tweets.text:
8/8

The share only beats bitcoin while bitcoin per share grows. So far that has only worked at a premium.

The July sale, the warrants and every company claim, checked:
tradingstrategies.work/blog/smarter...

#Investing

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
7/8

The holding has already paid once. On 23 July the company sold 177.89 BTC at $65,762, 39% below its average cost, to repay a $11.7m convertible loan two weeks early.

When the capital structure got tight, the bitcoin was the cash box.

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
6/8

On 14 Oct, new preferred shares started trading: 12% a year, paid weekly, cumulative.

That is £1.33m a year, 1.7 times the agency's annualised revenue. Bitcoin pays no interest, so the 12% comes from cash, new capital or the holding itself.

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
5/8

What £100 of bitcoin costs through the share on 15 Oct:

→ shares only               £101
→ plus debt and preferreds  £117
→ plus warrants             £125
→ net of all claims ahead   £130

25.8m of the 29.0m warrants, at 2.5p each, belong to the CEO and his wife.

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
4/8

In 2025 the engine ran on a premium. In nine tranches the company sold shares for £133.5m, from 16p up to £4.95.

Selling shares above bitcoin value raises bitcoin per share. In April 2026 the share traded at 0.75 of that value, and the company still sold shares.

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
3/8

Bitcoin per share, counting only shares actually sold:

→ 30 Apr 2026   905 sats
→ 15 Oct 2026   831 sats

The holding grew by 52 BTC, the share count by 11%. The company's own figure for Q3, its "BTC Yield", was −4.35%.

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
2/8

Behind the stock is a web agency in Guildford with £397,473 revenue and a £2.72m operating loss in the half-year to April.

It holds 2,830 BTC worth £172.8m, bought at about $108,500 on average. The agency is a footnote; the share is a bitcoin position.

tweets.author: tradingstrategies.work
tweets.text:
1/8

Smarter Web Company shares are bought to beat bitcoin: the London firm is meant to raise the bitcoin per share each year.

Its filings show the reverse: bitcoin per share fell 8.3% since April, and the share costs 30% more than its bitcoin.
